newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ debt markets end mixed after volatile day.
newsitem.headline: NZ debt markets end mixed after volatile day.

text.p: New Zealand debt markets closed mixed on Wednesday after a volatile session.
The 90-day bank bills retraced back to 90.60 percent from a low of 9.42 percent after the Reserve Bank of New Zealand ruled out any further easing in monetary policy for the time being.

Dealers said the announcement gave a bullish market a shock, and rates rose quickly on the back of it. Upside was limited, however, and although bill rates finished slightly higher they were seen easing back to 9.50 percent before the week's end.
Volume in futures was heavy once again. The front contract finished down 13 at 90.86.
The RBNZ statement put paid to a rally in the short and mid bonds, which closed flat. The 10-year bond rallied seven points on the day but still finished five points above its open.
"Really it just shows that yesterday's number wasn't the conclusive evidence they were after that inflation pressures were coming off," one money market dealer said.
He said traders saw the bank as comfortable with 90-day rates around 9.50 percent but believed it would probably not want to see them much lower.

The Reserve Bank on Tuesday said core inflation was 0.33 percent for the quarter, giving a 2.4 percent annual rise. The bank, which has a mandate to keep underlying inflation between 0-2 percent, had expected a 2.7 percent annual rise.

A spokesman for the RBNZ said in a statement on Wednesday the data were "markedly lower" than the bank predicted but it was only one indicator, and most of the deviation from forecast occurred in a single area.

Sources said the RBNZ was accurate on all its inflation forecasts apart from construction costs, which were out of line with past relationships and appeared to contradict housing consents data and anecdotal evidence about house prices.

The RBNZ said in September it needed to see conclusive evidence of slackening inflationary pressures before it eased conditions. Wednesday's statement made it clear the CPI figures had to be assessed in light of other emerging indicators.

New Zealand bonds ended mixed on spreads to other dollar bloc markets on Wednesday after a promising rally was nipped in the bud when the Reserve Bank ruled out any further easing in monetary conditions at this stage.

Aussie bonds remained softer as that market awaited the Reserve Bank of Australia's quarterly bulletin at 0500 GMT (6 pm NZT). NZ bonds outperformed Australia by almost 10 points in the longer maturities.
More emphasis has been placed on the RBA report than usual, as the market has priced in the expectation of a 50 basis point rate cut and is looking for confirmation of this view.
